minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee voted unanimously not to send its draft charter to the May Town Meeting
minutes.summary: The committee read its draft charter and a minority report, then heard written and spoken comment. Speakers mostly opposed an appointed town clerk, the select board name change, and new day-to-day language added to elected boards' sections, and many urged more time. Members agreed to keep working past May and voted unanimously not to present the draft; the next meeting date is to be set by poll.

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee voted unanimously not to present its draft charter to the May Town Meeting.
Members agreed to keep deliberating past the May Town Meeting rather than rush the draft.
The public hearing drew comment mostly against an appointed town clerk, the select board name change, and added day-to-day wording in elected boards' sections.
The library board chair asked that the library director, not the town manager, keep hiring library staff.
The next meeting date is to be set by a poll of members, posted 48 hours ahead, with an attempt to get it televised.

why_it_matters: The charter is the town's governing document, so changes to who is elected or appointed (such as the town clerk) and how boards are run would have gone to voters; none will be on the May Town Meeting warrant from this draft.
Residents who want a say still have time, since the committee plans to keep working and a later draft could return with revised wording on the contested sections.
